name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This exposes false positives and negatives without blocking work, giving us real data on its value. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR feedback, but it’s the only way to measure impact accurately. After two weeks, we’ll decide whether to keep it in parallel, drop it, or adjust settings based on the results.

name: Gauge
text: Running PR-Agent in parallel mode risks training the team to ignore *all* automated feedback—false positives and negatives alike. A better alternative: shadow mode on a random 20% of PRs, with manual review only on flagged changes, to isolate false negatives without drowning the team in noise. Settle it by tracking whether reviewers actually act on the feedback after two weeks—if adoption stays flat, the tool’s useless.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to have existing team norms, so noise won’t train anyone to ignore feedback. This cuts the cost of wasted reviews while still exposing false positives and negatives.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This gives us the full picture of false positives and negatives without cherry-picking contributors, so we see the tool’s real impact across the board. The trade-off is temporary noise in PR feedback, but that’s the price for accurate data—we can’t measure value if we half-test it. After two weeks, we’ll have hard numbers to decide whether to adopt it permanently or scrap it.
